title: The Immortal Finish
setup: Anderssen against Kieseritzky, London 1851. White has given away both rooks and a bishop. Count the finish before you count the material.
hint: Begin with a check. Then count the black king's squares, find the one black piece still guarding them, and give it something it must take.
explanation:
## The Idea

The Immortal Game, played in London in 1851: White is two rooks and a bishop down, and mates anyway.

{{Nxg7+}} takes a pawn with check, and {{Kd8}} is the only reply. Now c7 and e7 belong to the bishop on d6, and e8 to the knight on g7.

One black piece still guards e7: the knight on g8. {{Qf6+}} drags it off, because only that knight can answer the check. After {{Nxf6}}, {{Be7#}}, with the knight on d5 guarding the bishop.
